city_center.name: Downtown Tucson / Mission Garden
city_center.landmark: Santa Catalina Mountains to the north, Tucson Mountains to the west; Mission Garden at the foot of Sentinel Peak ('A' Mountain), the recreated birthplace of Tucson agriculture
city_center.notes: Mission Garden sits on the Santa Cruz riverbed where the Hohokam channeled water to grow crops thousands of years ago; it anchors Tucson's living food heritage. sources: Mission Garden (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Garden); visittucson.org City of Gastronomy.

featured_frontier.hook: Heritage White Sonora wheat + mesquite-flour Power Cakes with prickly-pear syrup, Santa Catalina foothills behind -- 4,000 years of Sonoran grain on the griddle
featured_frontier.photo_cue: mesquite + White Sonora wheat flour, prickly-pear syrup, adobe patio, Santa Catalina foothills
featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: heritage White Sonora wheat + mesquite flour + prickly pear (desert Sonoran food heritage)

cross_promo.partner: Mission Garden / Tucson City of Gastronomy heritage-grain growers
cross_promo.activation: heritage White Sonora wheat + mesquite-flour Power Cakes tie to the UNESCO City of Gastronomy grain story

audience: Sonoran-heritage food families, desert-foothills households; Fry's + Walmart + Costco shoppers, UNESCO City of Gastronomy food-culture town

cultural_notes: Tucson was named the first UNESCO City of Gastronomy in the United States in 2015, recognized for a food story dating back thousands of years and its Sonoran Mexican cuisine (source: Mission Garden, en.wikipedia.org; visittucson.org; unesco.org creative-cities/tucson)

Mission Garden, at the foot of Sentinel Peak, recreates the Santa Cruz riverbed cultivation where the Hohokam grew indigenous crops -- 'the birthplace of Tucson' (source: visittucson.org UNESCO City of Gastronomy; en.wikipedia.org Mission Garden)

heritage crops -- White Sonora wheat, tepary beans, mesquite flour, prickly pear -- anchor the local desert-adapted food identity (source: unesco.org creative-cities/tucson 300-year tradition of orchards and heritage foods)

the Pascua Yaqui Tribe and Tohono O'odham Nation are significant regional communities; any tribal food reference stays consent-gated -- no fabricated endorsement (INFERRED framing; verify + honor tribal sovereignty)

design_palette._provenance_note: adobe/mesquite/saguaro-rib grounded in Sonoran desert vernacular + Mission Garden heritage agriculture (visittucson.org; en.wikipedia.org Mission Garden). prickly-pear magenta + White Sonora wheat gold grounded in the heritage crops. hex values are perceptual approximations, not sampled -- flag for brand-fit review against the fixed Kodiak brand palette.
